item.title: Arknights: Endfield 1st Anniversary Festival Comes to Makuhari Messe on January 10-11, 2027
item.description:
The game launched on January 22, 2026 on PS5, PC, iOS and Android, and the festival was first confirmed in October alongside a newly drawn anniversary illustration. The official festival site now adds the schedule, ticket prices, attendee gifts and a first look at the venue.
The Endfield anniversary festival fills Halls 7 and 8 of the Makuhari Messe International Exhibition Hall in Chiba. Both days run from 10:00 to 18:00 JST, with last entry at 17:00. January 11 is a public holiday in Japan, so the event covers a full long weekend.
The venue map splits the space in two. Hall 7 holds the main stage and its seating area, the merchandise and capsule-toy zone, food stalls and a rest area. Hall 8 is given over to exhibits and attractions themed on places from the game, including Valley IV, Wuling and the Dijiang, with one more area still marked as coming soon.
Admission is split by day, so visitors need a ticket for each date they plan to attend. There are three ticket types:
The advance lottery runs from November 19 at 12:00 until November 29 at 23:59 JST, with results by email from December 3. General sales open on December 12, the same day the stage-seat lottery starts; that lottery closes on December 17 and results arrive on December 22.
Every visitor receives a set of attendee gifts: a shopper bag, an official guidebook, a metal-style poster, a clear card, a ribbon strap and a mirror acrylic ticket.
The venue shop will sell first-anniversary goods, with numbered tickets handed out inside the hall on the day. Most items will also go on sale by mail order after the event. A capsule-toy booth offers chibi acrylic keychains of ten characters at ¥600 per spin, with a limit of ten spins at a time.
The stage line-up, the full attraction list and the remaining area have not been revealed yet; GRYPHLINE says more details will follow on the Endfield anniversary festival site and on its Japanese X account, @AKEndfieldJP.

item.title: Lost Sword Opens Pre-Registration in Japan With a Free 5★ Kay and an Exclusive Costume
item.description:
Lost Sword is coming to Japan. Wemade Connect opened Lost Sword pre-registration for the Japanese version on November 18, 2026, on the App Store and Google Play, and every player who signs up before launch gets an exclusive costume for one of the game’s heroines.
The Arthurian action RPG is already live in other regions: the global version arrived on iOS and Android in July 2025. The Japanese edition gets its own official site and X account, @LostSword_JP, while a release date has not been announced yet.
The campaign runs from November 18 until the game launches, and rewards grow with the number of sign-ups. According to the official Japanese site, the milestones are:
Lost Sword retells the Arthurian legend with an all-girl cast. Excalibur, a holy sword forged by fairies, has vanished, and a prophecy says it will return to serve the true king once the red dragon’s protection fades. That protection ends when King Uther Pendragon falls to the rebel king Vortigern, and his daughter Elizabeth Pendragon goes missing while searching for the sword.
The player follows Ethan, a lifelong fantasy fan who once made fantasy games, alongside Morgana, a sharp-tongued ancient fairy bound to help him by a contract with Merlin. The roster on the Japanese site already lists more than 50 heroines, including Merlin, Guinevere, Lancelot, Gawain, Tristan and Jeanne d’Arc.
The Japanese pre-registration trailer introduces the cast and the round-table story:
Battles are real-time, 2D side-scrolling fights in which a party of heroines clears stages without stopping, with flashy skill animations for every heroine. Characters are pulled from the gacha and come in rarities up to 5★, and the game adds pets and ability cards on top of the team for extra strategy.
Outside combat, the Google Play listing mentions dungeons, solo raids and event dungeons, and the Japanese site shows a tavern where the heroines spend time between missions.
Lost Sword pre-registration is open now on the App Store and Google Play through the official site. Gacha Go! will report the release date once Wemade Connect announces it.

item.title: [OSHI NO KO] Puzzle Star Launches Worldwide on iOS and Android
item.description:
[OSHI NO KO] Puzzle Star, the official puzzle game based on the hit anime, is out now worldwide. The global version launched on November 18, 2026 on the App Store and Google Play, nine months after the game arrived in Japan.
It is available in English, Korean, Traditional Chinese and Simplified Chinese, in every region except Japan and a few other countries and regions. The game is developed by NHN, and KADOKAWA publishes the Japanese version.
The core is a block puzzle: you connect matching blocks to clear them and work through stages. The characters from the series do the heavy lifting, since each one brings its own skill and effects into a stage, so the team you take changes how you clear it.
Between stages, you place the characters in a lobby and dress them up in original outfits. New characters and outfits come as cards, which you pull in scouts, the game’s gacha. Many cards recreate memorable scenes from the TV anime, and in Japan the game has been running limited pickup scouts built around Kana, Akane and Ruby since its launch on February 25, 2026.
For the Oshi no Ko Puzzle Star global launch, new players receive a sign-up gift with stage items, a set of B-Komachi Ai decoration items and costumes, and diamonds for 10 scouts. The gift unlocks after you clear Stage 14.
KADOKAWA is marking the global release in the Japanese app too, with four campaigns:
The 50-second global trailer shows the puzzle boards with each character leading a stage, the cards you collect, Aqua trying on outfits in the dress-up screen and stills of scenes from the anime.
[OSHI NO KO] is the manga by Aka Akasaka and Mengo Yokozaki, with more than 23 million copies in circulation worldwide. The TV anime has a fourth and final season confirmed. The game is free to download from the official global site, which links to both stores.

item.title: hololive Dreams Wins Best Game in Google Play Best of 2026 Japan
item.description:
The Best App award went to the diet tracker Asken. Google also handed out six game category awards in Japan, and two of them went to gacha games: NTE: Neverness to Everness and Suikoden STAR LEAP.
hololive Dreams launched on July 23, 2026 on iOS, Android and Steam. It is the first official hololive smartphone game: players build a team from cards of the agency’s talents and play rhythm stages set to their original songs and covers, then spend time with the talents in a shared park full of minigames.
It got off to a fast start. Days after release it climbed to No. 1 on Google Play’s top-grossing chart in Japan, and Japan accounted for more than 70% of its downloads and revenue in the first month. In August the game passed 2 million downloads.
Since launch the game has kept adding to its park. The latest area, Soda Pop Lagoon, opened in September with a new team minigame. The card pool keeps growing too, and our hololive Dreams tier list ranks every card currently in the game.
Next to the overall Best Game, Google named one winner in each game category:
The full list, with the app awards, is on the official Google Japan blog.
Google Play also announced its 2026 winners in Taiwan the same day. There, Best Game of the Year went to Arknights: Endfield, praised for combining real-time strategy combat with base building. NTE won Best Cross-Device Game in Taiwan as well, giving it the same award in both markets. Best Story Game went to Chaos Zero Nightmare, The Battle Cats took the ongoing award again, and the indie award went to TOEM: A Photo Adventure.

item.title: The Seven Deadly Sins Arrive in Last Cloudia on November 19 With Meliodas, Merlin and Ban
item.description:
AIDIS’s pixel-art RPG Last Cloudia is teaming up with the TV anime The Seven Deadly Sins: Dragon’s Judgement. The crossover starts on November 19 in both the Japanese and the global versions, with Meliodas and Merlin as the first units and Ban joining a week later.
The lineup and the banner schedule were revealed in the official Last Cloudia TV broadcast on November 16. Merlin, voiced by Maaya Sakamoto, already has her own showcase video, while Ban’s kit is still under wraps. The dates and times below are the Japanese version’s (JST).
The collab is split into two halves. Meliodas and Merlin each get their own pickup banner from November 19, after maintenance, and Ban’s banner opens on November 26. All three close on December 10 at 12:59.
Each pickup comes with a paid step-up banner. The last step of its third lap guarantees the featured character, so Meliodas, Merlin and Ban can all be secured without relying on rates alone. The Boar Hat ark, named after Meliodas’s travelling tavern, is built to support counter-based units such as Meliodas himself.
Merlin is the first collab unit with a full showcase. Her video shows her new artwork and her pixel sprite in battle as an ice-element attacker.
Meliodas, the captain of the Sins, arrives alongside her on day one. Ban, the Fox’s Sin of Greed, is the only unit whose details have not been shown yet; AIDIS has only confirmed his banner and his ark, which shares its name with the order of knights itself.
Last Cloudia launched in Japan in April 2019 and is available on iOS, Android, DMM GAMES and Steam. The crossover lands while its 7.5-year anniversary festival is still running, which keeps adding a new reward quest every week for six weeks. Dragon’s Judgement is the final season of the anime adaptation of Nakaba Suzuki’s manga, covering the war against the Ten Commandments.

item.title: Harry Potter: Magic Awakened Will Shut Down on March 3, 2027 as Its Licence Expires
item.description:
Harry Potter: Magic Awakened is shutting down. NetEase announced on November 16, 2026 that the card-based RPG will end its service on March 3, 2027, when its game servers close for good. The reason given is the expiry of the licence agreement for the Wizarding World property.
The Magic Awakened end of service comes in two steps. On December 21, 2026, in-game purchases and new player registration end, and the game is pulled from every platform it is sold on. Players who already have it can keep logging in until the servers shut down on March 3.
Magic Awakened launched in China in September 2021 and reached the rest of the world in June 2023, on PC, iOS and Android. Players enrol at Hogwarts ten years after the fall of the Dark Lord, attend classes, join clubs and duel with decks of spell, companion and creature cards in real-time battles.
The game has already been through one shutdown. Its servers in the Americas, Europe and Oceania closed on October 29, 2024, while the Chinese and Asian versions kept running. The March 2027 date is the end of the line for what was left.
The announcement, posted on the game’s official Japanese X account, thanks players for “these five years” of exploring, growing and battling in the wizarding world, and says the team will stay with them until the final day. It adds that any change to the schedule, or further details on the closure, will come through NetEase’s official channels.
The notice does not mention refunds for unused premium currency. Any players still holding paid currency or passes should plan to spend them before December 21, when the shop closes. The game’s release trailer is a good reminder of the school life players are saying goodbye to.
That leaves a little over three months of play, and only five weeks to spend money in the game. After December 21 nobody new can join, so the final season belongs to the players who are already enrolled.
Magic Awakened joins the list of gacha games closing in early 2027. Every confirmed shutdown, with its final date and the regions it affects, is collected in our Gacha End of Service Tracker.

item.title: Jujutsu Kaisen Phantom Parade 3rd Anniversary: Itadori & Megumi Become the First Co-op Character, Gojo and Geto Follow
item.description:
The Phantom Parade 3rd anniversary plan covers the Japanese version of the game, which launched on November 21, 2023 and has passed 25 million downloads worldwide. It also brings two story events, one of them with a branching route through the Shibuya Incident, and a set of real-world promotions in Shibuya.
The 3rd Anniversary Gacha Part 1 runs from November 21 at 15:00 to January 3, 2027 at 14:59 (JST). Its headliner is SSR [Relentless Tandem] Yuji Itadori & Megumi Fushiguro (阿吽の猛攻), the first unit in the game where two characters share one slot and fight together.
Co-op characters get their own co-op skills. Using them alongside regular command skills fills a co-op gauge, and spending that gauge powers up the pair’s ultimate. The same banner adds a new SSR Recollection Bit with its own story, “Three Heads Make a Hungry Stomach” (3人寄れば腹が鳴る).
Two more anniversary banners follow. Part 2 brings SSR [Master of Space] Satoru Gojo (空間の支配) from November 30 to January 11, 2027, and Part 3 adds SSR [The Worst Curse User] Suguru Geto (最悪の呪詛師) from December 8 to January 11, 2027. Both start at 15:00 JST and end at 14:59.
That leaves all three anniversary banners running at the same time from December 8, so players saving for Gojo or Geto will want to plan their pulls before the Itadori and Megumi banner closes on January 3. For how the current roster stacks up, our Jujutsu Kaisen Phantom Parade tier list ranks the best characters for each team slot.
The celebrations start before the anniversary itself. The story event “Overlapping Twin Shadows” (重なる双影) opened on November 16 and runs until December 23. It centres on Itadori and Megumi, setting up the co-op unit, and its reward is the SSR Recollection Bit “Twilight Dash” (薄明の疾走).
The bigger story piece is “Where Truth and Lies Drift” (虚実の揺蕩う先は), a Shibuya Incident event split in two: the first half opens on November 21 and the second on November 26. Partway through, the scenario branches, and the choices players make change how the rest of the story plays out. Sumzap says more details will follow in-game and on the official X account.
Outside the game, the anniversary ties in with the Culling Game Part 1 anime. An ad truck featuring Naoya Zenin, who joined the game on October 30, drives around Shibuya from November 16 to 22, and free balloons of the shikigami Kogane are handed out in Shibuya from November 24 to 30.
The full 3rd Anniversary broadcast can be rewatched on the official YouTube channel until February 15, 2027, and the schedule is collected on the official 3rd Anniversary site. The English version of the game, published by Bilibili, runs on its own schedule.

item.title: Shangri-La Frontier: The Seven Colossi Delayed to Early 2027, With Unique Monster Raids Coming
item.description:
Shangri-La Frontier: The Seven Colossi will not launch in 2026. Netmarble announced on November 10 that the first game adaptation of Shangri-La Frontier is now aiming for early 2027, and that the new release window will be announced early next year. Pre-registration stays open, and every reward already earned through it carries over.
The news came in a letter from producer Kyung-ryul Kim, posted on the game’s official Japanese X account. The team had been working towards a 2026 release, but after the game’s first public showing at Tokyo Game Show it decided it needs more time to reach the quality and the amount of content players expect. With The Seven Colossi delayed, the letter also lists what is changing before launch.
The Tokyo Game Show 2026 demo, held from September 17, was the only time anyone outside Netmarble Nexus had played the game. Kim’s letter says the feedback from that booth drives the delay: players liked the 3D take on the original’s art, the speed of the combat and the voice acting, but the studio wants to rework several parts before it ships rather than release on the 2026 date it had been working towards.
The same producer letter went up on the English account on the same day, covering the feedback and the planned changes. The English version does not include the schedule paragraph, so the early 2027 target comes from the Japanese post.
The video above is Netmarble’s highlight reel from its Tokyo Game Show booth, where the game was playable for the first time. The demo put players up against Wethermon the Tombguard, one of the Unique Monsters from the original story, and Lycagon appeared in it too.
Kim’s letter names four areas the team is working on during the extra months:
Wethermon is one of the Seven Colossi that give the game its subtitle: the Unique Monsters that no player in the original story had managed to bring down before Sunraku. Netmarble says more details on both raid modes will follow in future announcements.
The game adapts Shangri-La Frontier, the web novel by Katarina that later became a manga drawn by Ryosuke Fuji and an anime, with 17 million copies sold worldwide. Players follow Sunraku, a gamer known for clearing broken “trash games” who takes on Shangri-La Frontier, a full-dive VR game of unusually high quality.
Netmarble Nexus is developing it for iOS, Android and PC. It is a tag-based collectible RPG: you build a line-up of characters from the series, fight with two on the field at a time and swap between them to chain attacks and guard against big hits. Battles are designed for one-handed play on a phone. We covered the first trailer and the Tokyo Game Show demo in September.
Netmarble has not named launch regions yet. The game has an English website and English social accounts, and pre-orders are open on the Japanese App Store. The new release window is due early next year.

item.title: Girls’ Frontline 2: Exilium 2nd Anniversary Update Lands November 19 With Koleda, 115+ Pulls and an SSSS.Gridman Collab
item.description:
Girls’ Frontline 2: Exilium celebrates two years of its global version with a major update on November 19. Sunborn and MICA Team revealed it in the 2nd Anniversary Special Preview Program on November 11: two new Elite Dolls, Koleda and Asteria, more than 115 pulls and 12,000+ Collapse Pieces in rewards, a new anniversary event and two collaborations, with DJMAX and SSSS.GRIDMAN.
The current Targeted Procurement banners close on November 18 at 18:59 (UTC-4), and the GFL2 2nd anniversary content runs until December 30. The game is free to play on iOS, Android and PC, and the full preview stream is on the official YouTube channel.
Koleda is a Vanguard and the former “Alpha” of Task Force DEFY, the role she handed to Alva. Long-time players know her as AK-12 from the first Girls’ Frontline. In combat she summons the Sinveiler, which pulls enemies in, attacks and splits the damage she takes. Her gear-shifting mechanic powers up the Sinveiler and raises both her survival and her damage.
Her Elite Weapon is Chernobog, an assault rifle that uses medium ammo and boosts Hydro damage and critical damage, both for Koleda and for her summons. Her character PV shows the Sinveiler in action:
The second Elite Doll arrives with the second half of the update on December 10. Asteria, ST AR-15 in the original game, is a Physical Support Doll. Her Elite Weapon is Compass of Penance. Both Dolls get their Covenant on the day they launch, and Peritya’s Covenant also goes live on November 19.
On top of that, the studio is giving away 1 pull and 800+ Collapse Pieces through its official social media channels until December 30, as announced on X. The stream also revealed three redeem codes that add up to 400 Collapse Pieces, 10,000 Analysis Blueprints, 10,000 Sardis Gold and 10,000 Combat Reports.
The anniversary event Tea Time Full of Memories starts on November 19. Players earn a special anniversary cake across the game’s content and give it to the Dolls of their choice. The story event Siege of Ilion comes out in three parts, the first from November 19 to December 9 and the last starting on December 17.
Alongside it come the second season of Frontier Expedition (November 19 to December 10, with no daily attempt limit), the return of Splash Arena on December 10, a party event on December 17 and the Gate of Wishes from December 26 to January 9. Two outfits are free: Acting Manager for Sharkry, earned through an event, and Budding Bunny Lady for Peritya. There are six new paid outfits, including Koleda’s beach look, Age of Spooms, which goes on sale with the update.
Older outfits also come back: a limited outfit rerun runs from November 19 to December 30.
The stream confirmed a collaboration with the rhythm game series DJMAX, with no date or details yet. It also revealed the first two Dolls from the SSSS.GRIDMAN collaboration, announced back at the 1.5 anniversary: Rikka Takarada and Akane Shinjo. The studio is planning both for 2027 in the global version.
The anniversary also reaches outside the game: a 2nd Anniversary Concert is set for December 20 at Kyung Hee University’s Peace Palace in Seoul, and the game will have a presence at Comiket in Tokyo from December 29 to 31.
